name: Question 19
problem: Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of ${x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$
worked_solution:
The standard Maclaurin expansion for $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯ \\  & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{120}-⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

To get an expansion for ${x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ we multiply this series by ${x}^{2}.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & ={x}^{2}(x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{6}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{120}-⋯) \\  & ={x}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{6}+\frac{{x}^{7}}{120}-⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 19
?

Find the first three non-zero terms of the Maclaurin expansion of x2sin⁡x.

a
x2sin⁡x=−x2+x46−x6120+⋯
b
x2sin⁡x=x3−x56+x7120−⋯
c
x2sin⁡x=1−x+x36−⋯
d
x2sin⁡x=x3+x512+x760+⋯
e
x2sin⁡x=x3−x624+x996−⋯
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The standard Maclaurin expansion for sin⁡x is sin⁡x=x−x33!+x55!−⋯=x−x36+x5120−⋯.

To get an expansion for x2sin⁡x, we multiply this series by x2. This gives x2sin⁡x=x2(x−x36+x5120−⋯)=x3−x56+x7120−⋯.
